scope: Mac experiment only. Production mask, coverage, footprint and CPU renderer compiled unchanged into scripts/ball-contact-crop. No app code changed. Not run on a phone.
question: Do zoomed crop masks at touches improve replacement edges?

zoomed_mask.decision: Not promoted. Sharper masks barely change what is drawn.

outlines.dataset: football-visible-real-008, 235 assistant-traced outlines, not blind reviewed

zoomed_mask.why: The image-edge fit sets the final circle; the mask only bounds it. Halo and shoe crescent are unchanged in freeze frames.

fake_blur.finding: When photographic calibration returns nothing, smear falls back to a box-stretch exposure guess. On sharp footage this blurs the print with no matching blur in the real ball, pulsing with ball speed.
fake_blur.conclusion: Removing smear is right on sharp clips and wrong on blurred ones. The existing edge blur detector cannot tell them apart: it finds none on IMG_1529, which has real blur. The real ball's own sharpness falloff with speed does separate these four clips (0.80 and above vs 0.15 and below).

not_fixed: Halo on one side of the ball
limitations: Four clips; the sharp/blurred split is a hypothesis until tested on more footage.
Sharpness is measured at 1080p on the Mac; the app's spin pass runs at 720p.
Sharpness compares a ball with itself between fast and slow frames; different prints are not compared.
IMG_8649 still pulses frame to frame (about 20%) with or without smear; cause unknown.
indoor1 ran without saved spin, so its print rotation differs from the app.

corrections: Fast vs slow sharpness (falloff) is too noisy across clips; along/across on fast frames replaces it.
IMG_1529 2.MOV is byte-identical to IMG_1529.MOV and has real blur at speed; it is not a sharp 60 fps sample.

exposure_estimate.method: Along/across gradient energy on the fastest frames, inverted through synthetic blur of the clip's own slow frames, divided by speed.
exposure_estimate.scoring_caveat: The first score compared raw print and real ball values and was invalid: a no-blur Arctic print reads about 1.4 to 1.5. The score was changed after seeing results to normalize each ball to its own no-blur value. Treat as a lead, not validation.
exposure_estimate.known_issue: One estimate exceeded a 60 fps frame and needs a clamp.
exposure_estimate.not_done: Not ported to the app. Not run on a phone.

app_code_results.scope: Real BallSurfaceTimeline.analyze and BallExposureEstimator on the Mac, 15 s of each clip. Not run on a phone.
